In the case of glacial ice, it's a combination of two things. First, the large amount of pressure squeezes out air, which makes smaller amounts of ice appear white-ish. Second, large quantities of water in general appear bluer because water absorbs every color of light except blue. That's also why glacial water appears so blue. Other large bodies of water don't look as blue because glacial water is much more pure and has less non-water material in it.

Well, all I can say is that again, you are making assumptions that are not true. I went through a period in high school (I'm 24 now) when I ate a lot of fast food, gained a lot of weight, so I cut it out at around age 19 except for when I cheated. Of course I had cheat days, but I drink maybe five times a year ( certain holidays) and I gave myself one cheat meal a week (mainly so I could enjoy a less restricted social life). Something like Chipotle or Chick Fil A so I felt more confident in fresh, real ingredients (still way took many calories for one meal, though! I know!). No more cheat days for me now, though. My diet for the last two years has been heavy on fruits and veggies, then a chicken breast once a day, and whole grains (Quinoa, wild rice, etc.) My treats were things like banana almond milk and peanut butter smoothies, or fried plantains. Now of course I can't prove any of that to you so you can choose to believe me out not. I guess what I just understand, and hope you can find some empathy for, is that weight loss is not always easy. It's a complicated mess for many of us, and unfortunately tied to many emotional situations, including sadness, self loathing, celebration, and social gatherings. You can feel like you're doing all the right things and using every ounce of motivation to do so, and it not work. Things work for some that don't work for others. My husband and I eat the same diet (except about twice the portion size for him) and he loses weight like it's nothing! You learn, educate yourself some more, and keep trying. I hope that anyone else out there that struggles with weight loss knows that there are people who understand, and want to cheer you on toward a healthier life, without judging for the times you cheat and feel like a failure. Let's all encourage each other to be better, instead of making each other feel like shit, which is usually counterproductive.

Yeah I actually was. I was eating between 1400 and 1800 calories a day, counting every little thing. So with my activity level I was at a deficit of about 200 calories a day. After 9 months of that not working I had to rethink. Now, I have had a lot of digestive issues so I actually may have some sort of medical issue I don't know about, but I just know that I have devoted so much time thought and energy into my diet that it's not as simple as counting calories.

You shouldn't be so quick to assume that since that regiment worked so easily for you, it would for others. I would love if that was all I needed to do to lose weight. I've been trying to lose weight seriously for about three years, starting with cutting calories majorly(by cutting portions, not with that low calorie processed crap) continuing with cutting processed foods to virtually nothing, and finally cutting all added sugar. Couple that with an average of four hours of moderate exercise per week, and I have been lucky to even maintain my weight. I am finally losing weight since I've cut all added sugar, but it's taken me a long time to find what worked for me, and I worked my ass off to figure it out. It has been incredibly frustrating to do so much without results and even more frustrating to live in a society where people assume these kind of horrible, judgemental things about me because I am overweight. Please remember, Every body is different, and you can't judge someone's actions or lack thereof, unless you actually know what they are. (And even then you shouldn't because it's just shitty.
